title: Bounded demotion policy with prefix quorums for KV cache correctness
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and long-lived prefix inference patterns are exposing a race between aggressive LRU/TTL eviction and in-flight KV usage on GPU. When a large micro-batch pins references across multiple CUDA kernels, a straight LRU or TTL eviction can free slots while the batch still needs them, causing either correctness violations (stale/missing KV lookups) or costly synchronous spills.

Proposal: Implement a 'bounded demotion' eviction path combined with a prefix quorum mechanism and batch-pin extension. Instead of immediately reclaiming a slot when it becomes eligible for eviction, we move it to a demoted slab with a demotion epoch and grace window. A prefix quorum (per tenant/prefix group) must observe unanimous demotable state before final reclamation, preventing cross-prefix races in continuous batching. Additionally, batches that reference KV entries will extend a 'pin' lease scoped to the batch epoch to prevent demotion during kernel windows.

The goal is to provide pragmatic correctness guarantees (no in-flight lookup fails, deterministic demotion progress) while keeping GPU footprint bounded and preserving throughput for small-latency requests.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests prove no KV lookup returns a missing entry when batch-pin is honored (fuzzed across interleavings)
Fuzzbench runs (existing harness) show zero linearizability violations for prefix-scoped operations under heavy continuous batching load
Memory reclamation latency stays within 1.5x of current best-case for steady-state workloads (measured on 80/20 seq length distribution)
99th-percentile token-latency regression <= 5% on our perf harness for standard demo models
Operational metrics and events emitted for demotion transitions (demoted->reclaimed) and prefix-quorum stalls
implementation_notes: Add two new allocation slabs: ACTIVE, DEMOTED. Demoted slab uses compact LRU but is excluded from immediate reuse until demotion_grace_ms expires or prefix quorum clears.

Introduce per-prefix DemotionEpoch counter stored with slot metadata (64-bit epoch + bitflags). In-flight pins include the epoch they observed; reclamation requires demotion_epoch > observed_epoch and grace window elapsed.

BatchPin extension: when a request enters continuous-batching pipeline, it registers pins for referenced prefixes. Pins are lightweight refcounts stored in shared host memory and atomically incremented/decremented around kernel launches.

Prefix quorum: each prefix group keeps a bloom-filter-like ack map across local partitions; final reclamation requires local partition to report 'no active pins' and global quorum (fast path) or delayed single-partition reclaim (slow path) to ensure progress.
Backpressure: when demoted slab high-watermark reached, we emit a scheduling signal to throttle admission of new large cross-prefix batches and trigger prefetch hints to avoid synchronous spills.
Telemetry: track demotion_count, reclamation_count, demotion_latency_ms, batch_pin_holds, and quota_throttle_events. Expose per-tenant breakdown in Console.
Make demotion_grace_ms tunable per deployment profile; default 50ms for hosted, 20ms for dedicated low-latency tier.
Add fast-path optimizations for single-prefix heavy workloads: if prefix ownership local and no multi-prefix crossing detected, bypass quorum and use local demotion to reduce latency.
testing_plan: Extend existing eviction fuzz harness to model continuous-batching: interleave pin acquisition, kernel delays, TTL ticks, and demotion triggers across 50k randomized trials
Unit tests for epoch monotonicity and demotion_idempotence (simulate restarts and partial failures)
Integration test in CI with real CUDA small model (gpt-mini) with synthetic workload that holds pins across kernel launches
Perf bench: run our 95/99th token latency and throughput sweep on runtime-1.22 branch, compare baseline and feature branch under scaled tenant mix
Chaos test: kill a partition leading to quorum lag and verify slow-path reclamation completes without stalls or leaks
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag kv.bounded_demotion.enabled=false by default
Canary deploy: enable on 5% of traffic in hosted for 48h, monitor demotion metrics and 99p latency
If canary stable, increase to 25% for 24h. Then enable for dedicated customers who opt-in with tuned grace window
After 7 days of stable telemetry, enable globally and bake into runtime-1.22 default config
Provide rollback knob to force immediate synchronous reclaim (for emergency memory pressure scenarios), with alerting when used
risks: Increased GPU memory usage due to demoted slab holding entries during grace window; worst-case could amplify tail pressure under pathological workloads
Quorum protocol increases cross-partition metadata traffic and complexity; buggy implementation could cause stalls or live locks
If batch-pin is not applied consistently across all batch codepaths (e.g., newer compiled kernels), we may still see race conditions
Operational complexity: tuning demotion_grace_ms per deployment adds knobs teams may misconfigure leading to regressions
notes: Related literature: 'lease-based cache eviction' papers and 'epoch-based reclamation' in concurrent data structures were used as references
We intentionally pick demotion+quorum vs global locks to preserve throughput for typical PLG workloads while protecting correctness in cross-prefix heavy cases
Design doc contains formal invariants (prefix atomicity, demotion idempotence, pin-safety) with small proof sketches
Coordination with SDK teams required: pin lease handshake must be exposed in low-level C API used by Python/Rust SDKs
